searchText: The snapshot is only for 128 states, the trie is by default for 10.000 blocks. You can do traces etc on the trie. If you do reorgs larger than 128, you need to rebuild the snapshot. If you need state beyond 10k blocks, you need to full sync and run an archive node If you want to trace stuff older than 128 blocks, you need to specify reexec in your trace command. There is documentation for that on thr website We don't prune transactions We only remove the index transaction -> block for transactions older than 1 year Yes, but only by knowing the blocknumber for the transaction Also you can change this by setting --txlookuplimit 0 You need to resync your node with that flag The transaction lookup by hash will not work. The lookup by block will iirc Eth_getblockbynumber( 0x123, true) will give you the full transactions of thag block You need to specify reexec as an optional parameter to the command I have no idea if ethers can do it though Geth can, please consult the tracing documentation for it Yes that should work Ah actually it might not work with pbss yet Hmm a hash based node should have no problem tracing this No the ability to reexec has been there for yeers https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/developers/evm-tracing yes Partial archive mode as suggested may be a possible improvement, but there are also possible protocol changes we’re looking at that may remove the archive-node requirement, e.g. by introducing a new output root version that can be included in the block-header, to avoid the historical data lookup entirely. the block header is more easily accessible for light nodes.
